topics.angle: how far away the Moon really is
facts: The average distance between Earth and the Moon is about 384,400 kilometres.
Moonlight takes about 1.3 seconds to reach Earth.
The Moon is slowly moving away from Earth, about 3.8 centimetres every year.

topics.angle: the sunlight you see is from the past
facts: Light from the Sun takes about 8 minutes and 20 seconds to reach Earth.
If the Sun disappeared, we would not notice for about 8 minutes.
The Sun holds about 99.8 percent of all the mass in the Solar System.

topics.angle: a day on Venus is longer than its year
facts: Venus takes about 243 Earth days to spin once on its axis.
Venus takes about 225 Earth days to orbit the Sun.
Venus spins backwards compared with most planets, so the Sun rises in the west there.

topics.angle: the biggest volcano in the Solar System
facts: Olympus Mons on Mars is the largest volcano in the Solar System.
It is about 22 kilometres high, roughly two and a half times the height of Mount Everest.
Its base is about 600 kilometres wide.
Saturn's average density is lower than the density of water.
Saturn's rings are made mostly of chunks of water ice and rock.
Saturn is the second largest planet in the Solar System.
